The '''Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation Limited''' ('''BBTC''') is an Indian [[trading company]] based in [[Mumbai]] owned by the [[Wadia Group]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-19 |title=Bombay Burmah to sell 3 tea estates in Tanzania for $1.2 million |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/bombay-burmah-to-sell-3-tea-estates-in-tanzania-for-12-million-16443981.htm |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Chengappa |first=Sangeetha |date=2021-06-06 |title=Wadia group's Bombay Burmah to exit plantations business |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/agri-business/bombay-burmah-to-exit-plantations-business/article34746623.ece |access-date=2023-05-09 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |language=en}}</ref> It was formed in 1863 by the [[Wallace Brothers]] of [[Scotland]]. It is [[List of oldest companies in India|India's oldest publicly traded company]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mudgill |first=Amit |title=Old isn't gold always! These 19th century firms failed to reward investors in last 5 years |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/old-isnt-gold-always-these-19th-century-firms-failed-to-reward-investors-in-last-5-years/articleshow/57746374.cms |access-date=2022-09-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation Ltd Share Price Today, BBTC Share Price NSE, BSE |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/stocks/bombay-burmah-trading-corporation-ltd-bbtc-share-price-361388 |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref> and was established to engage in the [[Myanmar|Burmese]] tea business through the initial step of taking over the Burmese assets of William Wallace.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-28 |title=Bombay Burmah shares hit fresh 52-week high; stock up 39% in a month; here's why |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/company-stock/story/bombay-burmah-shares-hit-fresh-52-week-high-stock-up-39-in-a-month-heres-why-435028-2024-06-28 |access-date=2024-09-21 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
The company's founding occurred when the six Wallace Brothers, originally members of a Scottish merchant house in [[Edinburgh]], first arrived in [[Bombay]] (now Mumbai) in the 1840s. A Bombay partnership was formed in 1848 as "Wallace Bros & Co". In the mid-1850s the Wallaces set up a business in [[Rangoon]], shipping tea to Bombay. In 1863 the business was floated as "The Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation". Its equity was held by both Indian merchants along with the Wallace Brothers, who had the controlling interests. By the 1870s the company was a leading producer of [[teak]] in [[Burma]] and [[Siam]], as well as having interests in cotton, oil exploration and shipping.

British motivations for the [[third Anglo-Burmese War]] were partly influenced by concerns of the BBTC. The Burmese state's conflict with the BBTC furnished British leaders with a pretext for conquest.<ref name="Webster1998">{{citation|author=Anthony Webster|title=Gentleman Capitalists: British Imperialism in Southeast Asia 1770-1890|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vH2ssfXKBLwC&pg=PA224|date=15 September 1998| publisher=I.B.Tauris|isbn=978-1-86064-171-8}}</ref>{{rp|224–225}} By the 1880s Wallace Brothers had become a leading financial house in London. This firm was able to affect the intelligence about Burma and, more critically, about the growing French influence in the country.<ref name="Webster1998"/>{{rp|227}}

The Vissanji family purchased the company from the Wallace brothers around the time of Indian independence. In 1992, the BBTC acquired and merged in [[BCL Springs]]. Later, BBTC was acquired by the [[Wadia]] group based in Bombay.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Verghese|first1=Luke|title=Bombay Burmah: A sprawling conglomerate|url=https://www.equitymaster.com/outsideview/detail.asp?date=09/13/2011&story=5&title=Bombay-Burmah-A-sprawling-conglomerate-Luke-Verghese|website=www.equitymaster.com/|accessdate=8 February 2017}}</ref>

Bombay Burmah, a part of the [[Wadia Group|Wadia group]], holds a majority share of 50.5 per cent in [[Britannia Industries]], amounting to a total of 12.17 crore [[Common stock|equity shares]]. <ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2023 |title=Bombay Burmah falls on sale of 3 tea estates in Tanzania |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/bombay-burmah-falls-on-sale-of-3-tea-estates-in-tanzania-10442751.html |website=moneycontrol.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-05 |title=Bombay Burmah to receive Rs 877 crore as interim dividend from Britannia Industries - shares jump 5% |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/bombay-burmah-877-crore-interim-dividend-from-britannia-industries-shares-rise-16338371.htm |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, the company announced that it will be divesting 3 tea estates in [[Tanzania]], measuring around 3,957 acres, to Udongo Wetu, Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-19 |title=Bombay Burmah to sell 3 tea estates in Tanzania for $1.2 million |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/bombay-burmah-to-sell-3-tea-estates-in-tanzania-for-12-million-16443981.htm |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref>

Orange County Resorts acquired eight coffee estates from Bombay Burmah for Rs 291 crore.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-01 |title=Bombay Burmah to sell eight coffee estates to Orange County Resorts for Rs 291 Cr |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/bombay-burmah-eight-coffee-estates-sale-291-crore-to-orange-county-resorts-16065501.htm |access-date=2023-05-06 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Controversies ==
In January 2025, Bombay Burmah Trading Corporation, along with its promoters including [[Nusli Wadia]] and his sons Ness and [[Jehangir Wadia]], and several affiliated entities, settled proceedings with the [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] (SEBI) over alleged regulatory violations. The matter involved alleged lapses in disclosures relating to shareholding changes and related-party transactions, including the classification of Wallace Brothers Trading & Industrial Ltd as a public shareholder despite its connection to the promoter group. SEBI noted that the indirect acquisition of an 8.11 per cent stake through Wallace triggered requirements for an open offer, which were not complied with at the time. The corporation and associated parties agreed to pay a total settlement amount of approximately Rs. 2.13 crore without admitting or denying the regulator’s findings, thereby concluding the proceedings.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 10, 2025 |title=Bombay Burmah Trading, Wadias settle matter with Sebi for Rs 2.1 crore |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/bombay-burmah-trading-wadias-settle-matter-with-sebi-for-rs-2-13-crore-125011001126_1.html |work=Business Standard}}</ref>
